cold_open.title: The Rented Throne
beats: Before the minions arrive, a confession from the Spire: the throne I sit upon is rented, and the lease came due this morning.
The bone-clerks brought the invoice on a silver tray, which was also rented, which was also on the invoice.
I opened the Grudge Ledger to record the insult, and found the landlord already listed. Page one. Underlined twice.
So I summoned him. The circle flared, the smoke rolled in, and out stepped a very tired skeleton holding a clipboard.
He was my own bone-clerk. I had sublet the throne to myself, through him, to save on paperwork. It cost me more paperwork.
We negotiated for three hours. He demanded dental cover. He has no gums. I granted it out of sheer administrative respect.
The throne stays. The clerk is now my landlord, my accountant and my only creditor, and he is sulking in the rafters.
cold_open.handoff: Which brings me to you, early arrivals: the throne needs witnesses, and witnesses get titles. Speak, and be recorded.

lines: Petition the throne: name one household object you would appoint to the Dread Council, and defend its credentials.
bits.payoff: The best object is sworn in with full ceremony and a better title than the minion who nominated it.

lines: The bone-clerks need a new motto for the Spire's front gate. Submit yours; the worst one gets carved anyway.
bits.payoff: He reads the worst motto aloud as if it were carved in obsidian, and orders it carved twice.

lines: Confess one small, petty grudge you hold, and I will judge whether it deserves a page in the Grudge Ledger.
bits.payoff: The pettiest grudge gets its own page, a wax seal and his personal endorsement.

lines: The budget allows exactly one new torch for the throne room. Make your case for which corner deserves the light.
bits.payoff: He awards the torch to the corner nobody argued for, because it was the cheapest to reach.

lines: A foil waits outside the summoning circle. Describe the most annoying hat it could be wearing, and I will judge the threat.
bits.payoff: He rates each hat as a hostile act and files the worst one under declarations of war.

lines: Invent a job title so specific and useless that even the Ninth Dark would refuse to fund it.
bits.payoff: He funds it anyway, out of spite, and appoints whoever invented it.

lines: Offer the worst possible name for a war horse, and I will decide which of my rivals deserves to ride it.
bits.payoff: The winning name goes to the Has-Been Hero's steed, effective immediately.

lines: The Lord's dispatch is late. Invent the excuse the courier will give, and I will rate it out of nine Darks.
bits.payoff: He accepts the most absurd excuse as plausible, then whispers an apology upward.

lines: The Investigation needs a name for its newest face-down card. Offer one, and the board will wear it until it is turned.
bits.payoff: He christens the fog with the best name and promises to clear it with evidence, not wishes.

lines: Grade my handwriting on the evidence seals: DOC, REP, CLM or SPC. Be honest; the clerks already laughed.
bits.payoff: He accepts the harshest grade with dignity and blames the quill's funding.

lines: Propose the official motto of the Ledger of Corrections. Accuracy is power, so the motto must be accurate too.
bits.payoff: He corrects the winning motto once, gleefully, and logs the correction.

lines: Describe the smell of an archive the bone-clerks have not opened in four hundred years. Wrong answers go in the margins.
bits.payoff: He declares the best description the official scent of due diligence.

lines: The camera that broadcasts my glory arrived with a warranty card sealed in red wax and great optimism.
The card promised to cover any damage caused by mortals, weather or acts of the Lord. I read the small print by lantern.
Exclusion seven: liches. Specifically liches. They had seen me coming from four centuries away.
bits.payoff: He frames exclusion seven behind the throne as proof that he is famous among vendors.

lines: My first Thrall saluted me with the wrong hand. I demanded an apology. He saluted again, with the other wrong hand.
We kept at it until sunrise. He has, it turns out, only wrong hands.
I promoted him to Deputy of Salutes on the spot, because consistency is the rarest virtue in any realm.
bits.payoff: The next minion to greet him is offered a seat beside the Deputy of Salutes, wrong hands welcome.

lines: A bone-clerk once filed himself under pending to avoid an audit. He stayed in the cabinet for ninety years.
When we found him he had annotated every folder around him, cross-referenced the lot and corrected two of my own claims.
I could not punish him. He was the best-sourced thing in the Spire.
bits.payoff: He dedicates tonight's first hex to that clerk and promises to grade it as carefully.

lines: In the Third Dark there was a lord who stamped DOC on everything, including his lunch.
The auditors came. They asked for the primary record of the lunch. He produced a sandwich.
The sandwich was downgraded to CLM, and so was he. That is why I respect the seals, minions.
bits.payoff: He invites the court to grade the next piece of evidence, sandwich standards applied.

lines: When the censor's bar slides across a thought tonight, I salute it through gritted teeth: it outranks me, and it knows it.
bits.payoff: He salutes the bar, sulks for one breath and moves on.

lines: The Grudge Ledger has a fresh page tonight, and it stays blank until someone in this room truly earns it.
Not by arriving. Not by typing my name. By doing something tonight the Spire will still resent next week.
bits.payoff: The first viewer to earn the page gets an entry built from what they actually did, read aloud once.

lines: A hex refuses to clear and the fog sits there, smug as a tax collector. The Spire files it as a setback, in ink it cannot afford.
bits.payoff: When the hex finally clears, he strikes the setback from the record with ceremony.

lines: Every audit costs candles, and the candle budget for tonight is one candle. We will be thorough, and we will be quick.
bits.payoff: When the case closes he snuffs the candle with ceremony and notes the savings in the Ledger.

connectors.line: Enough of my troubles. The throne room is filling, and I can hear minions breathing. Speak up.
The tale is told; now the court is in session. Who has come to kneel, and who has come to heckle?
So much for the lease. Now, to business: the court is open and the Grudge Ledger is hungry.
Hold that thought, minion; the throne has an item on the agenda.
A fine petition. It bears on a matter the bone-clerks raised this very morning.
Silence for a moment. The Spire has a tale that bears on this.
That is the tale. Now judge it, minions: was it a triumph or a budget problem?
Enough from the throne. The floor belongs to the court again.
The bit is done and the clerks are clapping politely. Your turn: what says the court?
The Plebiscite opens. Vote, and I shall obey the result with whatever dignity remains.
This is too important for one lich to decide. To the vote, minions; the count is sacred.
Let the court decide. The Plebiscite is open, and I am campaigning shamelessly for the first option.
The foil has worn out its welcome. The Investigation awaits, and the cards will not turn themselves.
Enough court for one night. The Investigation calls, and the bone-clerks have brought the case files.
Close the summoning circle. We move to the evidence board, where evidence is the only currency I accept.
